verdict.rationale: Checkout.com presents its Unified Payments API as giving "complete control of the entire payment lifecycle from a single API". Its docs cover API-driven payments, refunds, payment links, idempotent captures, voids and transfers, and Platforms sub-entity flows. It also explicitly states webhook configuration is manageable "using the Dashboard or the API", which is a concrete parity example. However, nothing states general Dashboard-to-API parity, and areas like risk rules and lists, reconciliation reports and Hosted Payments Page customization are not shown to be API-accessible. Missing for 10: an explicit API/Dashboard parity statement, evidence that risk rules, reporting and HPP management are available via API, and independent corroboration.
